title: Demand-Adjusted Opportunity Surface (DAOS) — token economics + latency elasticity
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Define and validate a reproducible prioritization surface (DAOS) that augments classic RICE with demand-weighted token economics and latency elasticity. The output will be a ranked list of roadmap initiatives (Q2 2026) that maps directly to OKRs and shows per-initiative expected unit cost delta, latency delta, and downstream revenue/engagement lift.

Problem: Standard RICE treats reach/impact/coefficient dimensions as static. For inference products the unit economics (tokens) and latency sensitivity vary widely across workloads — e.g., embeddings-heavy telemetry vs. low-latency chat. We need a single rubric that: 1) preserves RICE defensibility, 2) exposes token-driven marginal cost and latency-regression risk, and 3) ties to OKRs (latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, adoption).

Proposed DAOS approach (high-level):
1) Demand weighting: compute a demand vector per initiative based on traffic cohort projection (weighting by expected request volume, average prompt length, and embedding frequency).
2) Unit economics layer: estimate marginal cost per 1k tokens post-optimization (batching+quantization). Include conservative and optimistic quantization scenarios.
3) Latency elasticity: for each initiative, estimate user-facing latency sensitivity multiplier (0.0–2.0) drawn from historical features (chat vs. batch embed) and validated with feature flags / canary synthetic tests.
4) RICE fusion: compute base RICE score then multiply by demand-weight scalar and divide by cost-adjusted latency risk factor. Output: DAOS score and three interpretable axes (expected revenue lift, unit cost delta, latency risk).

Deliverables: scoring workbook (Google Sheets), algorithm notebook (Colab), PRD with acceptance criteria, sample prioritized roadmap (top 12 initiatives), and an evaluation harness to simulate budget-constrained tradeoffs.

Acceptance criteria:
- DAOS computed consistently for existing backlog of 60 initiatives.
- Top-5 ranked initiatives validated by two customer-facing PMs and one solutions engineer.
- Simulation shows at least one alternative prioritized set for each of three budget buckets (conservative/expected/aggressive).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Overfitting demand projections for nascent features — mitigate via conservative caps and sensitivity sweeps.
- Complexity may reduce stakeholder transparency — mitigate by providing both classic RICE columns plus DAOS score and a 1-page explainer.

Success metrics (mapped to OKRs):
- OKR: Reduce avg cost per generated 1k tokens by 8% (KR mapped to initiatives selected by DAOS).
- OKR: Improve P95 text-gen latency by 15ms for chat workloads (KR tied to latency-elasticity-ranked features).
- OKR: Increase paid user retention lift attributed to new inference features by 4%.

Next steps: workshop with Eng & SE to validate elasticity multipliers (2/26), build scoring workbook (due 3/8), run simulation and present to GTM on 3/22.
